title: U.S. House · Missouri's 3rd District
area: St. Charles and Lincoln counties and rural mid-Missouri counties along the Missouri River, including St. Peters, O'Fallon and Jefferson City-area communities.

context.text: Incumbent Bob Onder won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over John Fraser. Bethany Mann won the Democratic primary over Tommy Holstein and Paul Wilson. Jim Higgins advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Bob Onder

summary.text: Bob Onder is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 3rd District. A physician and attorney who ran an allergy and asthma practice for more than 30 years, he served in the Missouri House and, from 2015 to 2023, the Missouri Senate before being elected to Congress in 2024; he sits on the Judiciary, Transportation and Infrastructure, and Education and Workforce committees.

background.text: Born January 6, 1962; graduated from St. Louis University High School in 1980.

Earned a bachelor's degree in economics and biology from Washington University in St. Louis (1983), an M.D. from Washington University School of Medicine (1987), and a J.D. from Saint Louis University School of Law.
Opened a private practice in 1992 specializing in allergy, asthma and clinical immunology, where he says he served patients for over 30 years, and also ran a small business.
Elected to the Missouri House of Representatives in 2006 (District 13) and served one term, 2007 to 2009; he authored a 2008 law barring sanctuary cities in Missouri.
Left the state House to run for Missouri's 9th Congressional District in 2008 and lost the Republican primary to Blaine Luetkemeyer.

Elected to the Missouri Senate in 2014 and re-elected in 2018, serving from 2015 until he was term-limited in 2022; he was Assistant Majority Floor Leader, chaired the General Laws Committee and was vice chair of the Judiciary Committee.
In the Senate, pushed the 2019 Missouri Stands for the Unborn Act, which banned abortion at eight weeks of pregnancy or later and was signed by Gov. Mike Parson.
Withdrew from the 2022 Republican primary for St. Charles County Executive, and entered the 2024 race for Lieutenant Governor before leaving it to run for Congress.

Won a seven-candidate 2024 Republican primary for Missouri's 3rd District after Rep. Blaine Luetkemeyer announced he would not run again, and won the general election with 61.3% of the vote; sworn in January 3, 2025.
According to his House biography, lives in St. Charles County with his wife, Allison; they have six adult children.

priorities.text: Official House issues page lists Congress, economy/jobs, education, energy, military and veterans, pro-life, agriculture, immigration and the Second Amendment as his stated issue priorities.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a "steadfast champion of Pro-Life legislation" and is a cosponsor of the Born Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act.

Says he will "vigorously fight on behalf of gun owners and the Second Amendment" in Congress, citing his role in passing Missouri's Constitutional Carry law and Second Amendment Preservation Act as a state senator.

As a Missouri House member, sponsored and passed HB1549 (2008) to ban sanctuary cities, penalize employers who hire undocumented workers, and end "catch-and-release"; the Federation for American Immigration Reform called it the strongest state anti-illegal-immigration law in the country.

record.text: As a member of the Missouri House, sponsored and passed HB1549 (2008), a state ban on sanctuary cities.
As a Missouri state senator, led passage of the state's Constitutional Carry law (2016) and Second Amendment Preservation Act (2019), and sponsored legislation expanding the Castle Doctrine.
Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Bethany Mann

summary.text: Bethany Mann is the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 3rd District. An environmental chemist who has tested for contaminants including PFAS, she previously ran for the seat in 2022 and 2024 and is campaigning on science-based policy, rural infrastructure investment and healthcare access.

background.text: Born in Normal, Illinois; was homeschooled and attended Wright City High School in Missouri.
Earned an associate degree from Lincoln Land Community College (2008) and a bachelor's degree from the University of Illinois Springfield (2010).

Describes herself as an environmental chemist and technology professional, a working mother of three and a lifelong Missourian, with work in agriculture, energy and water infrastructure including testing for contaminants such as PFAS; Ballotpedia lists projects with the EPA and USDA.
Serves on the executive board of the Kansas Laboratory Education Association and as Vice Chair of the Missouri Democrats LGBTQIA+ Caucus.
Is the daughter of an Air Force veteran and granddaughter of a WWII veteran, according to her Ballotpedia survey.
Was the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 3rd District in 2022, losing to Blaine Luetkemeyer with 34.9% of the vote, and again in 2024, losing to Bob Onder with 35.3%.
Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 69.1% of the vote over Tommy Holstein and Paul Wilson.

priorities.text: Economic opportunity and infrastructure: investing in union-led jobs in clean energy and agricultural technology, modernizing rural broadband, energy resilience and clean water access.
Accountability: protecting reproductive freedom, safeguarding voting rights and ensuring equitably funded public schools.
Rural healthcare: strengthening rural hospitals and expanding access through mobile clinics, telehealth and incentives to retain rural medical staff.

positions.summary: Lists defending abortion access as essential healthcare among her healthcare priorities.
Supports Medicare/Healthcare for All to eliminate financial barriers to care.
Calls for holding corporate polluters accountable and creating union-led jobs in clean energy and rural broadband as part of modernizing infrastructure.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions drawn from her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
